title: Storytelling Through Art
subtitle: Four beats, and the gap that does the work.
objectives: Order the parts of a visual story
Name the parts of a comic page
Explain what the gap between panels does
Name key figures in Philippine komiks

cards.title: A story in pictures is a story in decisions
cards.text: Which moment do you draw? Which do you leave out? A comic page is mostly the moments the artist decided not to show.

cards.title: Four beats in any visual story
cards.text: Comic, storyboard, film or game cutscene. The same four.
points: **Setup**: who, where, and what is at stake.
**Turning point**: it could go either way.

cards.title: Four panels, and what each order would mean
cards.text: Four panels, one story. Pick panel 1 and see what each order would mean.

question.text: Which beat is the moment it could go either way?
question.explain: Without it, the ending has nothing at stake.

cards.title: What the parts are called
cards.text: The vocabulary is small and the test uses it.
points: **Speech balloon**: what is said. **Caption**. What is narrated.
**Splash**: a single panel filling the page.

cards.title: The gutter does the work
cards.text: Nothing is drawn in the gap, and that is where the reader does the most.
points: **Panel 2:** the other fighter is on the canvas.
**You saw the punch.** It was never drawn.
**The reader fills the gutter.** That is the trick of the form.

question.explain: The reader supplies what happens in it.

cards.title: Three names worth knowing
cards.text: Komiks were the most-read medium in the country for decades.
points: **Francisco V. Coching**: called the dean of Filipino illustrators.

cards.title: A storyboard is a game before it exists
cards.text: Nothing gets built until somebody draws the sequence.
points: **The order is tested on paper** because paper is cheap.

cards.title: A fight is already four beats
cards.text: Which is why it is the easiest thing to storyboard.

cards.title: Four empty panels
cards.alt: An open sketchbook ruled into four empty comic panels with a pencil and eraser beside it
cards.text: This is the whole form. The gaps between them are where the reader works.

cards.title: What to remember
points: The reader fills the gutter. The best moment is often not drawn.
Velasquez, Ravelo, Coching: the names Philippine komiks is built on.

teacher.summary: Term 2 Week 6 MAPEH, Arts strand. The interactive is the lesson here: he sequences four panels himself and each wrong order is answered with what that order would mean rather than with a cross, which is both the house rule on wrong answers and the truth about storytelling. The vocabulary card is short because the test uses only five words. The gutter card carries the real idea of the form (the reader supplies the punch) and it transfers straight to storyboarding, which is why the gaming lens follows it. Philippine komiks gets three names, which is what a Grade 6 paper asks for.
discussion: Ask which four beats a film he likes has.
Ask what happens in the gutter.
Ask why a storyboard is drawn before anything is built.
Ask which panel he would leave out, and why.
extension: Have him draw four panels of something that happened this week.
Have him retell a story leaving out the turning point and see what breaks.
misconceptions: "Every moment has to be drawn." The best ones often are not.
"A caption and a balloon are the same." Spoken against narrated.
"Komiks were a small thing here." They were the most-read medium for decades.
